material_events.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Risk Factors, filed 2026-05-21)
material_events.claim: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted, materially reducing the future availability of Section 48E and 45Y tax credits that Nextpower's customers rely upon for qualified solar facilities, requiring projects to begin construction by July 4, 2026 for a continuity safe harbor or be placed in service by December 31, 2027.
quotes: On July 4, 2025, a U.S. federal budget reconciliation bill known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA") was enacted. The OBBBA, among other things, materially changed most of the federal renewable energy incentives, including those described in Sections 45X, 48E, and 45Y.

the OBBBA substantially reduced this timeframe to require that projects begin construction by July 4, 2026 to utilize a continuity safe harbor that permits solar projects to be placed in service within four calendar years following the calendar year in which the project began construction for tax credit eligibility. Alternatively, solar projects that begin construction after July 4, 2026 must be placed in service by December 31, 2027 to qualify for the Section 48E and 45Y credits.
